3D-Printed Servo Arms

Design Objective

Three custom mechanical arms were designed to connect the servomotors to the yarn-selection mechanism. Each arm converts the angular position of one servo into the displacement required to activate or release one colour channel.

The use of custom components makes it possible to:

  • adapt the actuator geometry to the machine structure;
  • obtain repeatable motion for the three yarn channels;
  • reproduce the mechanism through 3D printing;
  • calibrate mechanical movement through firmware angles.

Servo Association

Mechanical actuator Electrical actuator ESP32 command
Yarn-selection arm 1 Servo 1 on GPIO13 C1
Yarn-selection arm 2 Servo 2 on GPIO14 C2
Yarn-selection arm 3 Servo 3 on GPIO27 C3

Active and Inactive Positions

The firmware defines two positions for each printed arm:

  • DOWN: inactive position, used when the corresponding yarn channel is not selected;
  • UP: active position, used when that yarn channel must participate in the current pixel.

At the current calibration stage the initial values are:

Arm DOWN UP
Arm 1 60° 140°
Arm 2 60° 140°
Arm 3 60° 140°

These values are initial experimental settings and should be refined after final assembly.

Recommended Assembly and Calibration Procedure

  1. Keep yarns disconnected during the first powered test.
  2. Power the servo supply and run a command that sends all servos to DOWN.
  3. Mount each printed arm in the intended inactive orientation.
  4. Send C1, C2 and C3 individually.
  5. Check that each arm moves without collisions or excessive mechanical force.
  6. Modify the UP_n and DOWN_n angles in servo_switch_usb.ino if necessary.
  7. Repeat the test with the complete three-arm assembly.
  8. Connect the yarns only after safe motion has been confirmed.

Safety Note

During first tests, the printed arms must be free to move and must not be forced against a mechanical stop. A blocked servo can draw excessive current and damage the actuator or the printed part.
